title: Steve Hilton in Fresno County promotes $3 gas plan as election nears

 Steve Hilton in Fresno County promotes $3 gas plan as election nears 
 Republican gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton brought his campaign to Fresno County on Thursday, offering local drivers discounted gasoline while making his case to voters just days before Election Day. KFSN By Vincent Camarillo Friday, October 30, 2026 12:16AM Share FRESNO COUNTY, Calif. (KFSN) -- Republican gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton brought his campaign to Fresno County on Thursday, offering local drivers discounted gasoline while making his case to voters days before Election Day.
 The campaign stop at the Loma Vista Travel Plaza offered gasoline at $3 per gallon to 150 drivers, a promotion Hilton described as a preview of what Californians could expect under his policies if elected governor.
 Sources tell Action News Hilton's campaign paid the difference to make the $3 price possible.
 For many residents, the temporary relief was welcome amid ongoing cost-of-living concerns.
 "The way everything is right now, we're either debating putting gas, or buying food, or paying my bills, or paying rent," said driver Charlotte.
 Vehicles lined up at the station as residents took advantage of the discounted fuel.
 "I'm a family of six. We have four young children under the age of 18, so the cost of things, sporting events, it's a lot harder for us to be able to get to where we gotta go if we're paying the price that we are," said Lorna, another attendee.
 RELATED: Xavier Becerra, Steve Hilton clash over key issues in California gubernatorial debate 
 Hilton said he would work to permanently lower fuel costs by reducing what he describes as hidden gas taxes, easing regulations and increasing California oil production.
 "The gas tax itself, you're right. That needs legislation. Those other three things: the hidden gas taxes, the regulations, and the California production. All three of those, I can do," Hilton said.
 The Republican candidate also promoted a proposal to cap vehicle registration fees at $73.

 When asked how the state would offset the lost revenue and whether taxpayers could face higher costs elsewhere, Hilton pointed to a budget restructuring plan.
 "We've set out a plan, actually, to increase the budget of the California Highway Patrol and transfer it to the general fund," he said.
 Democratic candidate Xavier Becerra's campaign criticized Hilton's proposals, issuing a statement that read: "Donald Trump keeps driving up costs, and his lapdog Steve Hilton keeps applauding. Xavier Becerra spent the last decade making health care and prescription drugs more affordable. Becerra is ready to lead California forward."
 The campaign event came as new polling from the Public Policy Institute of California showed Becerra leading Hilton among likely voters statewide.
 Despite those numbers, Hilton expressed confidence in his chances.
 "I think there's something happening that the polls aren't picking up, but it's not gonna happen unless people vote," he said.
 With just days remaining before the election, candidates from both parties continue making their final appeals to voters across California as the race for governor enters its closing stretch.
